# Evidence grading rubric

Loaded only when the skill reaches step 4 - an example of progressive disclosure:
the agent does not pay for this text until it needs it.

| Grade    | When to use it                                                                 |
|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Strong   | n >= 10 samples or cells, realistic test conditions, and replicated by another group or batch |
| Moderate | n >= 5, OR realistic conditions without replication                            |
| Weak     | n < 5, a single batch, simulation only, or idealised conditions (e.g. coin cells at low pressure when the claim is about pouch cells) |

Downgrade one level if:
- the main mechanism is inferred from simulation rather than measured;
- the paper itself lists the result as preliminary or calls for replication.

When two papers disagree, prefer the one tested under conditions closer to the
user's question, then the one with the larger sample.
